headline: iCloud storage notification glitch puts unremovable red badge on Settings app
summary: An annoying bug on iOS 27 is causing an unremovable red notification badge to appear on the Settings app for some users, tied to iCloud storage suggestions.
details: Some iPhone users on iOS 27 are experiencing a persistent notification glitch, where the Settings app displays an unremovable red badge. This visual alert indicates an issue or pending action within the app, but in this case, it's a false positive.

The bug is specifically linked to iCloud storage suggestions, prompting users to activate or upgrade their storage. Even after interacting with the suggestion or ensuring iCloud is set up, the red badge remains stubbornly present.

This persistent notification is causing frustration among affected users, as it cannot be dismissed through normal means. It creates a constant visual distraction, suggesting an unresolved issue that isn't actually there.
Currently, there is no official fix or workaround from Apple for this particular glitch. Users are hoping for a resolution in an upcoming iOS update to remove the erroneous badge.

headline_marked: [[Glasshouse v0.1 Is Out]]: A Memory Benchmark for AI Systems
headline: Glasshouse v0.1 Is Out: A Memory Benchmark for AI Systems
summary: Glasshouse v0.1 aims to solve common issues with AI memory benchmarks, providing a consistent and verifiable method for comparing system performance. It addresses discrepancies where vendor numbers often don't match independent measurements.
details: Glasshouse v0.1 has been released as a new long-term memory benchmark for AI systems. It directly tackles long-standing problems in developer communities, such as inconsistent vendor-published numbers and results that vary significantly based on the grading model used.

The benchmark's development incorporated extensive feedback from developer communities, including suggestions gathered from Reddit. This collaborative approach led to the inclusion of features like the stale fact axis, contradiction axis, and false memory probes, all designed to improve accuracy and reliability.

Individuals are encouraged to run the benchmark and submit pull requests or issues if they find any discrepancies. Companies can also submit their results or add their company details, with comprehensive instructions available in the project's repository.

All necessary information, including how to run Glasshouse v0.1, is publicly available on GitHub at github.com/wontopos/glasshouse. The creators explicitly welcome feedback on any numbers that appear incorrect, aiming for continuous improvement and transparency.
